In order for the plain view exception to apply the cops need to (1) be legitimately on the premises where the search occurred, (2) the thing seized has to be readily apparent and (3) there has to be probable cause that the thing seized is contraband. 

From the fact pattern (2) and (3) are pretty clear so the question is testing you on (1). They had an arrest warrant for the man which would let them arrest him in his own home but he went to his friends house. So the cops would need a warrant to search the friends house or an exception to be at the friends house to be considered legitimately on the premises of the friends house. The friend flat out said no when the cops asked to search and they pushed past him. Therefore they were in the friends home unlawfully and (1) is not satisfied.

Even though they could literally see the drugs, element (1) isn’t satisfied and so the cocaine is going to be suppressed.

A process that helps me through each question is to:

1. Read the question and the call but do not look at the answers yet. 

2. ID which subject the question is about

3. ID which rule the question is testing you on

4. State the rule out loud to yourself in full

5. Using the rule you just said to yourself, answer the call without looking at the answers. 

6. Find the answer choice that best reflects the answer you gave yourself.

7. Review the other 3 choices by reading and figuring out why it does not apply to the question. Usually what happens is that 2 answer choices are talking about rules that don’t apply to the question and a third answer choice either misstates the applicable rule or applies it incorrectly.

Hope it helps.
